articles.h1: Ollie vs The Farmer's Dog: what each brand publishes about price, checked 2026-09-26
articles.lede: Quick answer: the two brands do not publish the same kind of number, so a straight price-versus-price verdict does not exist on their own sites. The Farmer's Dog prints one figure - plans start at about $2/day, with delivery options mostly ranging from 1 week to 2 months of food and including free shipping. Ollie prints per-meal figures instead - Full Fresh Meals from $1.57 a meal, Half Fresh Plan from $1.00 a meal - and answers in per-day terms only inside its FAQ: food starts at less than four dollars a day for small dogs fed Ollie exclusively, and averages $8 a day. Neither brand prices your dog on a public page (Ollie uses its plan builder, The Farmer's Dog uses a questionnaire), so the numbers below are floors, not bills. Every line carries its official source and a check date of 2026-09-26.

The two publish different units (per meal versus per day), each prices your dog individually through its own tool, and neither brand publishes a head-to-head figure for the same dog. Anyone quoting a single winner is doing arithmetic the brands themselves do not do.

blocks.h2: How this page was checked
blocks.html:
This page is a read-out, not an opinion. On 2026-09-26 (UTC+8) we fetched Ollie's Meal Plans page in raw HTML at 19:06, opened The Farmer's Dog's FAQ and Ollie's FAQ in a real browser at 19:10, and re-read Ollie's homepage at 19:21 - then opened Ollie's FAQ answers one question at a time (cost, billing, cancellation, storage, shipping), because the answers are loaded on click and do not appear in the page source.

What that produced: one per-day number from The Farmer's Dog, two per-meal numbers plus two per-day numbers from Ollie, and a set of terms (shipping, cancellation, storage, billing) that are simply printed differently by each brand. Where a brand does not publish something, the cell says so instead of guessing.

Deliberately excluded: every third-party comparison table, every crowd-sourced price, and every conversion between units that the brands themselves never print.

blocks.h2: The exclusive bit: each brand publishes the number the other one does not
blocks.html:
This is the whole comparison in one line: only The Farmer's Dog publishes a per-day starting price, and only Ollie publishes per-meal starting prices. That is not a stylistic quirk - it changes what you can honestly calculate.

Ollie gives you $1.57 and $1.00 but no official meals-per-day figure, so the public pages never multiply them out; its per-day answer lives in a separate FAQ entry ($8 average, under $4 for small dogs). The Farmer's Dog gives you about $2 a day and never prints a per-meal number anywhere on its FAQ. So a reader who types 'Ollie vs The Farmer's Dog price' into a search box will find sites doing the multiplication for them; the brands do not.

The terms diverge in the same pattern. Ollie pins down the mechanics to the day (charged three days before shipping, freezer life of 6 months unopened, 4 days once thawed, cancel on the website but not the app) while The Farmer's Dog keeps it loose (pause, cancel, reactivate anytime; food below 40°F on arrival; delivery from 1 week to 2 months). Neither is wrong - they are just different disclosures, and both are printed in the sources linked beside each row.

faqs.q: How much does JustFoodForDogs cost?
faqs.a: It publishes shelf prices rather than a quote: $153.99 for Chicken & Rice, $167.99 for Turkey & Whole Wheat Macaroni and $181.99 for Beef & Russet Potato, each for a 14-pack of 18-oz packs. Larger boxes cost more on the same pages - 21-packs at $230.99, $251.99 and $272.99, 28-packs at $307.99, $335.99 and $363.99, and 8-packs of 72 oz at $287.99, $311.99 and $335.99.

faqs.q: Is the JustFoodForDogs subscription really 50% off?
faqs.a: On the check date the subscription option on all three recipe pages showed 50% off the 14-pack - $77.00, $84.00 and $91.00 against compare-at prices of $153.99, $167.99 and $181.99 - and the site banner read '50% Off First Subscription Order + Free Shipping'. The official terms qualify it: 50% off your first subscription order up to a $139 maximum discount, one per household, continental U.S. only, subject to change without notice.

faqs.q: What discount do I get after the first JustFoodForDogs order?
faqs.a: 5% off all subsequent subscription orders, stated on the same official promotion page as the first-order offer. It is the only written ongoing discount the brand publishes - the first order's 50% is capped at a $139 maximum discount.

faqs.q: How much is JustFoodForDogs shipping?
faqs.a: Free on orders over $49, calculated after discounts and before tax, and first-time subscription orders are eligible for free shipping too. Below that threshold the flat fee is $19.99, frozen and dry goods ship separately with separate charges, and there is no delivery to PO Boxes, APOs or FPOs.

faqs.q: Can you cancel a JustFoodForDogs subscription anytime?
faqs.a: Its terms say 'You may cancel your Autoship at any time' - with one condition: cancel before the Autoship renews, otherwise the next order is billed. You cancel from your account, and the payment processor charges your first order at placement and then at the frequency you chose until you cancel.

faqs.q: How long does JustFoodForDogs food keep?
faqs.a: Up to 18 months (547 days) in the freezer for frozen packs. Once thawed, non-fish meals stay fresh sealed for up to 7 days and 5 days after opening; fish-based recipes keep 5 days sealed and 3 days once opened. The FAQ says to thaw in the refrigerator - about 24 hours for an 18-oz pack - and never to refreeze thawed food.

faqs.q: Is JustFoodForDogs suitable for puppies?
faqs.a: It depends on the recipe. The Chicken & Rice page says the recipe is formulated to meet the AAFCO Dog Nutrient Profiles for all life stages, including growth of large size dogs, and marks it perfect for puppies and adult dogs. The Turkey & Whole Wheat Macaroni and Beef & Russet Potato pages state their feeding trials substantiate nutrition for adult maintenance, and the Beef page says it is not intended for growing puppies.

faqs.q: Does JustFoodForDogs use preservatives?
faqs.a: Its FAQ answers plainly: 'Our only preservative is the freezer. We do not add any preservatives at all.' The product pages separately print 'No Additives, Preservatives, or Added Growth Hormones', and the FAQ says canine diets are balanced to NRC standards and then tested through AAFCO feeding trials.

faqs.q: Where is JustFoodForDogs made?
faqs.a: In open-to-the-public kitchens customers can visit, plus the company's own kitchen in Irvine, California, according to its FAQ. The site also lists a store locator for pickup, but the pages read on 2026-09-27 do not print a pickup price list, so this page prices only what is published online.

faqs.q: Do you need a vet's prescription to order?
faqs.a: The pages read on 2026-09-27 print no veterinary sign-up or prescription requirement for these Fresh Frozen recipes - the FAQ instead documents its AAFCO and NRC nutrition standards, and its Vet Portal and Targeted Nutrition lines are listed separately on the site.

blocks.h2: How this page was checked
blocks.html:
On 2026-09-27 (UTC+8) we fetched the three Fresh Frozen recipe product pages and the Shop All collection page in raw HTML, and read the FAQ, the Offers, Coupons & Promotion Details page and the terms of service directly. Variant prices were taken from each page's own product data, not from a screenshot or a listing elsewhere.

The finding worth keeping: JustFoodForDogs is the only brand in this comparison that lets you price an order before handing over your dog's details - and it is also the only one that writes down what happens after the first order (5% off every later subscription order). The 50% headline has a written ceiling: $139.

Deliberately left out: any per-day or per-serving cost (the brand publishes no per-day figure), any price from a retailer or marketplace, any stock or delivery estimate, and any figure that does not appear on an official page linked below.

blocks.h2: What the review comes down to
blocks.html:
Strip the copy back and the brand discloses four things most competitors do not. Every box size is priced publicly - 14, 21 and 28 packs of 18 oz, plus the 8-pack of 72 oz, on the recipe's own page. The subscription discount is written down: 50% off the first subscription order capped at $139, free shipping with it, and 5% off every order after that. Shipping has a number attached - free over $49, $19.99 below it. Storage has numbers attached too - 18 months frozen, 7 days sealed after thawing, 5 days once opened.

The differences between recipes are narrower than the price gap suggests: the real switches are life stage (Chicken & Rice covers all life stages including large-breed growth, the other two are maintenance recipes and the Beef page warns against growing puppies) and calories per pack - 774, 882 and 792 kcal per 18 oz.
